name: Sharing-Sensitive Counters and Capture Avoidance in Higher-Order Rewriting
description: Shows shared-policy counters orient embedded beta steps while tree barriers do not lift unqualified. Full capture is blocked with decidable capture checks and an eight-row closeout catalog.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: A counter reading only the argument branch of an application under the shared policy, and one reading only the continuation of a share node under explicit sharing, orient the duplicating recursor step, refuting any lift of the tree barrier to every policy; no direct measure orients duplicating beta, the beta-compatible counter fails on a beta step, and capture avoidance fails without freshness of the binder in the body and holds with it, with exact decidable gates on the binder-free, share-free fragment.
summary: The theory studies higher-order rewriting with sharing, beta and binder policies, closed fragments, duplicating recursor steps, beta steps and policy-sensitive counters. The questions are orientation of each policy's steps, the lift of the tree barrier to every policy, orientation of beta steps, capture avoidance, and orientation of duplicating beta by direct measures. The shared counter, which counts only the argument branch of an application, and the explicit-sharing counter, which counts only the continuation of a share node, orient their rewrite steps, every non-tree sharing policy orients the imported duplicating step, and embedded shareApp-recur terms have strictly smaller counters than recur-succ terms. The unqualified sharing and rewriting lifts are therefore false; the beta-compatible policy fails to orient every beta step; no direct measure, additive over application, transparent under lambda and zero on variables, orients all duplicating beta steps; and a variable-constant measure at constant c orients duplicating beta exactly if all its values lie below 2c, while no such measure orients it. The capture-avoidance law without freshness of the binder in the body is refuted by a counterexample, its body-fresh variant is proved, the occurrence, freshness and capture-safe gates are exact on the binder-free and share-free obligations, and the certified fragment succeeds. An eight-row policy audit, a closeout with total row evidence, and the sharing-boundary and rewriting final catalogs record these orientations and blockages, mark full higher-order rewriting as outside, and yield no unrestricted impossibility.
boundary: Under the shared and explicit-sharing policies every duplicating and rewrite step strictly decreases the policy counter, so the claim that no policy admits an orienting counter is false; the files of this theory prove no nonorientation theorem for the tree policy, which enters only through that refuted lift. Duplicating beta resists every direct measure, with the variable-constant case reduced to the threshold 2c, and the beta-compatible counter fails on an explicit beta step. Capture avoidance fails without freshness of the binder in the body and holds with it, and the closeout marks full higher-order rewriting as outside, so the blocked rows give no unrestricted impossibility.

conclusions.statement: PolicyOrientsStep holds for sharedPolicy and for explicitSharingPolicy, so every rewrite step for each policy strictly decreases its policy counter.
For every sharing policy, if it is not a no-sharing tree-only policy then its counter orients every duplicating step.
The unqualified higher-order lift claim is false.
The unqualified higher-order rewriting lift claim is false, so no unrestricted impossibility theorem follows from the blocked full-capture row.
For every direct measure M, with no positivity or pump hypothesis, M does not orient duplicating beta.
For any constant c and any variable-constant measure M at c, with no range hypothesis, M does not orient duplicating beta.
For a variable-constant measure M at constant c, M orients duplicating beta if and only if every term t satisfies M.eval t < 2 * c.
It is false that the beta-compatible policy orients every beta step.
There exist beta-related terms where the beta-compatible counter does not strictly decrease.
Every beta step is a rewrite step for the beta-compatible policy.

For all shared terms b, s and n, the shared-policy counter is strictly smaller on the boundary-embedded shareApp-recur term than on the boundary-embedded recur-succ term, and the explicit-sharing counter is strictly smaller on the corresponding embedded shareApp-recur term than on the embedded recur-succ term.
The full-capture capture-avoidance law as stated is false.
Given binder-distinctness, freshness, and binder-free and share-free hypotheses on argument and body, the capture-safe check succeeds.

For every name and term t, the occurrence classifier returns true if and only if FreeVarOccurs holds, and for every name, binder name, argument and body, the capture gate returns true if and only if distinctness, freshness and binder-free and share-free conditions hold on argument and body.
For every closeout row its indexed evidence proposition holds, and the sharing-boundary and rewriting final catalog records hold.

openPoints: Descent under a binder requires binder distinctness and argument freshness, with binder-free and share-free side conditions for the executable gates.
Plugging and substitution closure hold only for binder-free contexts and closed fragments under their stated closedness and freshness hypotheses.

Executable capture gates are sound and complete only on the exact obligation surface of binder-free and share-free terms, while full capture-avoiding semantics stays explicitly open and full higher-order rewriting is marked outside the catalog.
Blocking the full-capture interface does not yield an unrestricted impossibility, since the unqualified lift claims are themselves refuted.

The conditional variable-constant no-go carries an unbounded-range hypothesis while the arbitrary-constant and zero-constant versions need no range hypothesis, and orientation would require all values below twice the constant which additivity defeats.
Blocked closeout tags record refuted target interfaces rather than open problems, with no row left open.

subTopics.name: Rewriting syntax, steps and beta binders

files.summary: The file classifies the two sharing policies with a singleton no-sharing predicate containing only tree. It proves every non-tree policy orients the imported step and that the shared branch refutes the unqualified lift claim. It shows embedded shared terms carry the closed first-order shape and assembles the boundary status.
files.conclusion: Every policy outside the singleton tree class orients the step, refuting the unqualified no-go claim.

files.summary: The file adds beta steps, contextual closure, free-variable and freshness predicates and binder-free contexts. It proves substitution and plugging preserve the prior closed fragment and freshness under the stated hypotheses. It gives an identity-redex counterexample showing the beta-compatible counter does not orient beta steps and packages the branch split.
files.conclusion: Beta steps embed in the rewrite relation but the beta-compatible counter does not orient them.

files.summary: The file defines a policy-indexed higher-order rewrite step and policy-sensitive counter with an orientation predicate and an overclaiming universal lift statement. It proves shared and explicit-sharing counters orient their branches and that steps embed from prior carriers. The shared orienter refutes the unqualified lift claim.
files.conclusion: The shared orienter defeats the claim that no higher-order policy orients its steps.

files.summary: The file adds executable occurrence, freshness and gate classifiers with option-valued substitution checks. It proves classifier and gate equivalences, soundness and totality on the exact obligation surface, and preservation of binder, share and beta freeness. It records the full capture-semantics boundary and assembles the decidable catalog.
files.conclusion: The executable capture checks succeed exactly on the stated obligation surface and preserve freeness, with full capture semantics recorded as the open boundary.

files.summary: Defines binder-free, share-free and beta-free predicates over higher-order terms, with linear and DAG-shared abbreviations, beta-free contexts, and capture-safe and context-safe substitution obligations. Introduces direct additive measures that are additive on application, transparent through binders and zero on variables, plus a variable-constant generalization with value c on variables. Proves the pointwise orientation condition is equivalent to eval t < 2 * c, that app (var 0) (var 0) attains 2 * c, and hence no member orients all duplicating beta steps, unconditionally for every c and via an adapter for the zero-variable class. Packages the inhabitation, threshold and no-go results into variable-constant and universal boundary certificates and a capture-subfamily catalog.
files.conclusion: No direct measure and no variable-constant measure at any constant c orients all duplicating beta steps.

files.summary: Re-exports the eight-row policy taxonomy as closeout rows with projected statuses and indexed row evidence. Proves the row list has length eight, is duplicate-free, never uses the open tag, and that every row carries its evidence proposition, with the full-capture row backed by avoidance-law refutation, target-interface refutation and direct-measure no-gos. Records that the blocked full-capture row does not yield an unrestricted higher-order impossibility, since that universal nonorientation claim is itself refuted, and packages all rows into a closeout catalog.
files.conclusion: The eight-row closeout catalog holds with total evidence, blocked full-capture justification, and no unrestricted higher-order impossibility.

files.summary: Defines Boolean classifiers isLam, binderFree, shareFree, betaFree, linear, dagShared and context classifiers that mirror the Prop predicates. Proves each classifier returns true exactly when the corresponding Prop holds, provides Decidable instances derived from those equivalences, and shows closed fragments and embeddings satisfy the relevant classifiers with plug-preservation. Packages the equivalences and closure facts into a decidable-classifier catalog.
files.conclusion: Every Prop subfamily predicate has a correct Boolean classifier with Decidable instances and plug-preservation, packaged in a classifier catalog.

files.summary: Packages the M2 rewriting layer into a single catalog recording transported restricted-fragment and no-sharing results, shared and explicit-sharing orienting counters with their counterexamples, binder-free substitution and context closure, beta-step transport and contextual closure, freshness obligations, and the beta-compatible counterexample with its non-orientation blocker. Provides the canonical catalog value and projection theorems that recover each component, including classifier equivalences, subfamily closures and the audit, full-capture and closeout catalogs. States the typed obstruction to an unqualified higher-order lift.
files.conclusion: The canonical M2 rewriting catalog holds, transporting restricted results and blocking the unqualified higher-order lift.

files.summary: Enumerates seven full-capture requirement rows with declared statuses and defines the strong capture-avoidance law, its body-fresh repaired variant, the certified-fragment checker interface and the conjunctive target interface. Proves the body-fresh variant holds, exhibits a concrete counterexample refuting the strong law, proves checker success on binder-free and share-free inputs, and refutes the orientation and target interfaces while re-exporting the exact counterexample boundary. Collects the refutations and variable-constant and direct-measure no-gos into a blocked-row justification and a full-capture boundary catalog, explicitly noting that blocking does not give an unrestricted impossibility.
files.conclusion: The strong capture-avoidance and full-capture target interfaces are refuted while the body-fresh law and certified checker fragment hold.

files.summary: Defines the eight higher-order policy rows and five status tags with the row list and per-row status assignment, keeping statuses as data separate from semantic content. Defines the indexed evidence family assigning each row its proposition and proves it total, with the full-capture row carrying the exact boundary plus universal and conditional variable-constant no-gos and the unrestricted row carrying the refutation of the universal lift claim. Packages row enumeration facts and representative evidence into a policy-audit catalog.
files.conclusion: Every one of the eight policy rows carries its evidence proposition, with blocked tags backed by refutations rather than openness.

files.summary: Defines sharing, beta and binder metadata tags with tree, shared, explicit-sharing and beta-compatible policy fixtures, and an untyped term syntax with variables, atom, successor, application, lambda, recursor and sharing nodes. Defines the var- and lam-free closed fragment, a binder-shadowing substitution without renaming that may capture, one-hole contexts with plugging, and embeddings from the sharing-boundary syntax and shared terms, each proved to land in the closed fragment.
files.conclusion: The rewriting syntax, closed fragment, substitution, contexts and embeddings are defined with closure of embeddings in the fragment.

files.summary: Defines a minimal higher-order carrier with a closed fragment, a policy-indexed duplicating recursor step, and a policy-sensitive counter that counts both application branches under tree semantics but only the continuation under shared semantics. Proves the shared counter agrees with the first-order shared counter on the embedding, transports shared steps, strictly decreases on shared duplicating steps, and recovers the sharing counterexample. Concludes the shared orienter refutes any unqualified claim that the tree barrier lifts unchanged to every sharing policy.
files.conclusion: The shared-policy counter orients all shared duplicating steps, refuting any unqualified lift of the tree barrier to every policy.

files.summary: This file is a stable API layer over two validated catalogs for higher-order sharing and rewriting. It aliases policies, terms, contexts, steps, counters, fragments and classifiers, and re-exports the final catalogs through projection theorems. It states shared and explicit-sharing counterexamples and blockers against unqualified lifts, plus beta, capture, classifier and subfamily projections.
files.conclusion: The file exposes the validated M2 sharing-boundary and rewriting catalogs, their shared and explicit-sharing counterexamples, and the blockers against unqualified lifts as a stable API.

files.summary: This file packages two imported sharing barriers with a typed scope marker. It defines the final catalog record and proves it from imported orientation, counterexample, lift-blocker and no-sharing results. Its projections expose the shared counterexample, the unqualified-lift blocker, the no-sharing requirement, and the marker that full higher-order rewriting is not claimed.
files.conclusion: The final catalog packages the shared-policy orientation, its counterexample, the unqualified-lift blocker, the no-sharing requirement and the outside-catalog marker in one record.

files.summary: This reach file checks the beta-binder layer, including binder-aware and binder-free substitution, beta steps, freshness, closed-fragment closure and policy-counter facts. Four examples witness the hole context, branch-split status, failure of the beta-compatible policy to orient steps and an explicit counterexample pair.
files.conclusion: Binder-free closure holds while the beta-compatible policy does not orient beta steps, witnessed by an explicit counterexample.

files.summary: This reach file checks the higher-order boundary layer, from sharing, beta and binder modes and policies to embedding, counters and catalog transports. Five examples project the subfamily status, tree and sharing witnesses, the explicit-sharing counterexample inequality and the block on unqualified lifting.
files.conclusion: Restricted fragments transport while the shared policy blocks any unqualified higher-order lift.

files.summary: This reach file checks decidable capture gates, including free-variable and freshness classifiers, summaries, safety gates and their exactness with obligation preservation. Three examples project the decidable catalog and the success of capture-safe and context-safe checks under their obligations.
files.conclusion: Decidable capture-safe and context-safe checks succeed exactly under their obligations and preserve freeness.

files.summary: This reach file checks higher-order capture subfamilies, including binder, share and beta-free predicates, linearity, DAG sharing, obligations and the beta counterexample package with catalog status. It also checks the direct and var-constant measure families, unbounded inhabitants, threshold characterizations and no-go theorems with axiom footprints. Fifteen examples gate catalog existence, closed-fragment properties, embeddings and the conditional versus unconditional orientation failures.
files.conclusion: Closed share-free fragments embed linearly while no direct or var-constant measure orients duplicating beta, with an exact two-times-constant threshold.

files.summary: This reach file checks the higher-order closeout catalog, including row taxonomy, statuses, total evidence and the preserved full-capture avoidance block. Eight examples gate the catalog, its full-capture and unrestricted projections, status equalities, evidence totality and the non-claim of unrestricted impossibility.
files.conclusion: The closeout catalog is total with full capture theorem-blocked and no unrestricted higher-order impossibility claimed.

files.summary: This reach file checks decidable classifiers for lam, binder, share and beta-free, linear and DAG-shared predicates with context variants and exactness lemmas. Three examples project the classifier catalog and decidability instances for binder-free terms and beta-free contexts.
files.conclusion: All stated higher-order predicates are decidably classified with exactness and closed-fragment implications.

files.summary: This reach file checks the final higher-order catalog that aggregates transports, substitutions, beta facts, subfamilies, decidable and capture-decidable catalogs, audits and closeout with all projections. Twenty-two examples project each component, from no-sharing transport and substitution closure to classifier exactness, counterexample preservation and lift blocking.
files.conclusion: The final catalog projects every earlier transport, classifier, counterexample and blocked claim into one closed package.

files.summary: This reach file checks the full-capture boundary, including rows, avoidance law, syntax carrier, substitution semantics, sharing evidence and blocked orientation and target interfaces with catalog status. Twelve examples gate the catalog, upstream obligation, blocked laws, exact boundary status, a concrete freshness fact and the blocked-justification components without upgrading to unrestricted impossibility.
files.conclusion: Full capture is theorem-blocked with body-freshness repair, without yielding any unrestricted higher-order impossibility.

files.summary: This reach file checks the higher-order policy audit, including the eight-row taxonomy, statuses, total evidence and full-capture and unrestricted row facts. Eight examples gate the catalog, length, nodup, open witness, theorem-blocked full capture, never-open status, evidence totality and the unrestricted refutation.
files.conclusion: All eight policy rows are audited with none open and full capture theorem-blocked.

files.summary: This file exercises the public API for higher-order sharing boundaries and its rewriting counterpart. It instantiates final catalogs, subfamily, decidability, audit and closeout catalogs, classifier correctness lemmas, closure and substitution lemmas, and policy branches for tree, shared, explicit-sharing and beta-compatible policies. It also checks the shared-policy counter, the unqualified lift blockers, the beta-compatible counterexample and restricted-fragment transports.
files.conclusion: Unqualified higher-order and rewriting lifts are blocked while restricted tree fragments transport and close.

files.summary: This file checks projections from the higher-order sharing final catalog and the outside-catalog marker. It verifies the shared orientation and counter inequality, the unqualified lift blocker, the no-sharing status with its rejection, lift-hypothesis and restricted-fragment components, and the full higher-order outside marker. It also checks that the marker is definitionally the negated lift claim and audits axioms.
files.conclusion: The final catalog projects the shared counterexample, the lift blocker and the no-sharing requirement while marking full higher-order rewriting as outside.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the higher-order sharing boundary interface. It verifies that embedded shared steps decrease the shared policy counter, that the shared recursor shape yields a closed fragment, and that the unqualified lift claim is contradictory. It also checks the higher-order recovery inequality that breaks the tree barrier.
files.conclusion: The shared policy orients embedded steps with a decreasing counter while the unqualified higher-order lift claim is contradictory.
